ci-bot: [CI PERF] PR #18021 — microperf_pipeline failed: benchmark=single_sequence_throughput, threshold diff -4.1% (expected >= -2.0). Artifacts: https://ci.redwood.example/18021/artifacts :warning:

eva: saw this on merge check. PR touches kernel selector and batcher window. cc @sam @liam

sam: fyi I ran the same microbench locally, saw similar drop. tail latency +25ms. quick output:
```
bench: single_sequence_throughput
baseline: 3200 tokens/s
current: 3072 tokens/s
delta: -4.0%
hotspot: kernel_selector::choose_kernel_for_seq_len
```

maria: flamegraph on the CI artifact shows a bigger hotloop in kv_cache::lookup on the warm path. snippet: 
```
kv_cache::lookup 45%
kernel_selector::score 20%
batcher::maybe_merge 10%
others 25%
```

liam: interesting — PR also changed preferred kernel ordering for int8 path. that could change memory access patterns and cause KV thrash on GPU. anyone repro with nvprof / CUPTI?

eva: repro with perf builds + CUPTI attached, top GPU kernels are:
```
gpu_kernel: quant_matmul 38%
gpu_kernel: kv_read 30%
kernel_dispatcher 12%
```

sam: sounds like the prefetch heuristic change increased average batch fanout which increases concurrent KV reads -> more misses. batcher telemetry?

maria: confirmed: before merge median batch=3, after merge median batch=6 on the CI harness (50k runs sample).

sam: try forcing the old kernel order to confirm hypothesis:
```
export REDWOOD_KERNEL_ORDER=legacy
./bench/microbench --bench single_sequence_throughput
```

eva: ran that on the same CI image — result returned to baseline within noise (+0.3%). so kernel order change is the likely root cause.

ci-bot: Tagging PR as :rollout-blocker:.

liam: bisect plan: revert only the kernel-order patch from PR (keep batching heuristic). can someone open a targeted revert? @maria?

maria: opened revert PR #18022: https://git.redwood.example/p/r/18022 — focuses on kernel order only.

ops-bot: Scheduled rollback on "shadow" lane and will re-run microbench after merge.

sam: follow-up: we should add a microbench golden that asserts no >2% regression when kernel-order flips for int8 fallbacks. filed issue #430.

eva: I'll add a unit that pins kernel order for the int8 fallback path and a small telemetry patch that logs batcher fanout correlated with kernel choice.

maria: thanks — monitoring CI. :eyes:

ci-bot: Revert PR #18022 merged, re-running microbench...

ci-bot: CI verdict: PASS. bench delta +0.1% — unblocked. :tada:

maria: marking incident resolved and will follow up with a short postmortem and a note in the PR about adding the golden test."
